column1: # rename-aliases.tsv — registry of old-term identifiers (the rename plans alias registry).
# Read by scripts/docs/check-old-terms.sh: an identifier listed here may still be used;
# any other identifier fails on an added line that has LEG_ or CONSOLE_ at a word start, BANK, OVERNIGHT, a bare WAVE or _WAVE, SEQUENCE_,
# or HIMMEL_WORKER_ not followed by SESSION_. A direction of keep marks a name owned elsewhere that is never renamed.
# Columns (tab-separated): old, new, kind, direction, slice, remove-at.
# new/slice/remove-at read pending-N2892 until the polished plan fixes the new names.
# kind: identifier (a name on the lint's list), prose (a word the operator renamed), env (one variable), env-prefix
# (a prefix ending in _), marker (a status token), do-not-rename (a name kept as is).
# direction: old-to-new | keep for identifier, marker and do-not-rename; warn | fail for prose; for env and env-prefix
# the scripts/lib/env-alias.sh function that resolves OLD against NEW: restrict (env_alias_restrict, a guard ON switch),
# permit (env_alias_permit, an *_OK override), value (alias_env, a path, model or timeout).
# First match wins: the R1 block below lists every exact name above the prefix that would swallow it, then the
# identifier rows follow alphabetically. scripts/lib/test-rename-aliases.sh pins the R1 block.
